facts.text: Fields Corner takes its name from Zechariah Field, an early 17th‑century settler who arrived in Boston in 1629.
Founded in June 1630, Fields Corner is one of Boston’s oldest commercial districts.
Between 2005 and 2010, the Dorchester Avenue Project poured $18 million into widening sidewalks, adding bike lanes and installing energy‑efficient lighting in Fields Corner.
The Fields Corner MBTA station opened on November 5, 1927, becoming the southern terminus of the Red Line’s Dorchester extension.
In 2002, Viet‑AID built an 18,000‑square‑foot community center that now hosts cultural events, youth programs and small‑business support.
The 1874 Municipal Building, a Victorian Gothic structure designed by George Clough, once housed a police station, courthouse, and even a jail.
